sections.name: File setup, Lap
sections.title: Lap record shape and header
sections.what: Describes one lap: its number, its time in seconds, and whether it is an out-lap from the pits.
sections.why: Likely reason: the filter needs these fields to find clean laps.
sections.watch_out: Times must be in seconds, since mixing units would give a meaningless slope.

sections.name: degradation
sections.title: Tyre wear rate
sections.what: Removes out-laps and very slow laps, then fits a line through the rest to find seconds lost per lap. Returns the slope and how many laps were used, or zero if fewer than two remain.
sections.why: Likely reason: a line fit smooths out lap-to-lap noise.
sections.watch_out: Zero is returned when there is too little data, which looks the same as no wear, so check the laps used count.

sections.name: pitWindow
sections.title: Best pit lap
sections.what: Finds the first lap of the stint where the cumulative time lost to wear is at least the pit-lane loss, using a direct formula. Returns nothing if wear is not growing, otherwise the lap, the laps into the stint, and the loss at that lap.
sections.why: Likely reason: a direct formula avoids looping through every lap.
sections.watch_out: Assumes wear grows by the same amount each lap, so fuel burn or sudden tyre falloff would move the real window.

summary: Estimates how fast a car's tyres lose time within a stint, and the lap where time lost to worn tyres outweighs the time lost in the pits.
purpose: Helps The Professor work out a pit-stop window.
why: The header calls it an illustrative tool that models tyre wear as a straight-line trend.
how: Removes out-laps and very slow laps (over 107 percent of the fastest), fits a straight line of lap time against lap number to find seconds lost per lap, then finds the first lap where the cumulative loss reaches the pit-lane loss.
inputs: A list of laps with lap number, time in seconds and an out-lap flag, plus the stint start lap, the pit-lane loss and the wear slope.
outputs: The wear slope and how many laps were used. The pit window, or nothing if wear is not growing.
risks: Assumes wear is a straight line and grows evenly, which real tyres do not always do. Fewer than two usable laps gives a slope of zero.
debug: If the window is missing, check the slope is positive. If the slope looks odd, check the out-lap flags and the 107 percent filter.
